_meta.source: English variant of the curated operation-template dataset. It keeps the same stable IDs and technical configuration as operation_templates.json.
_meta.note: operation.end_date_days is resolved to an absolute ISO date at use time by apate.web._operation_templates.resolve_operation_fields().
_meta.localization: Parallel localized files were chosen instead of language keys in every string. The web wizard and examples/seed_demo.py retain one unchanged schema, while template IDs, TTPs, plugin IDs, kinds, hostnames, addresses, and other technical values remain literal and identical across locales.

templates.summary: Early detection of a known espionage actor seeking to move laterally to the financial segment through SSH brute force.

operation.name: APT28 — Lateral movement to the financial segment
operation.adversary_motivation: Espionage and access to financial data in the corporate segment
operation.target_assets: Financial network segment, Internal file servers
operation.adversary_notes: Profile based on TTPs publicly attributed to APT28 (curated MITRE ATT&CK catalog from apate.attack).
operation.narrative_description: The decoys simulate a recently migrated staging environment with weak configurations typical of a pre-production environment.
operation.psychological_impact: The adversary believes they have found a low-risk environment from which to move laterally to real financial systems without being detected.
operation.roles:
SOC lead: N. Pérez
Threat analyst: M. Gómez

scenario.description: Detect port scanning and SSH brute force targeting the financial segment

plugins.expected_adversary_belief: The SSH decoy server is a real jump host into the financial network.
plugins.expected_adversary_action: Attempt brute force and, if successful, move laterally from there.
plugins.success_metric: Alert in under 10 minutes from the first login attempt.
plugins.Description: SSH decoy gateway to the financial segment

templates.summary: Intelligence collection on a known fraud actor impersonating outsourced remote support for HR.

operation.name: FIN7 — Remote support impersonation in HR
operation.adversary_motivation: Financial fraud through compromise of remote support accounts
operation.adversary_notes: Profile based on TTPs publicly attributed to FIN7 (curated MITRE ATT&CK catalog from apate.attack).
operation.narrative_description: The user profiles simulate remote support employees with predictable behavior patterns and reused credentials.
operation.psychological_impact: The adversary believes they are interacting with real low-privilege accounts with operational mistakes typical of an outsourced provider.
operation.roles:
Identity analyst: L. Fernández
HR lead: C. Ibarra

scenario.description: Detect brute force and exploitation of an exposed application against support accounts

plugins.expected_adversary_belief: The remote support accounts are real and have legitimate access to internal systems.
plugins.expected_adversary_action: Use compromised credentials to access systems and escalate privileges.
plugins.success_metric: Detect access outside the simulated behavior pattern in under 1 hour.

templates.summary: Control validation against exfiltration by combining network and behavioral decoys during the quarter close.

operation.name: Lazarus Group — Control validation against exfiltration
operation.adversary_notes: Profile based on TTPs publicly attributed to Lazarus Group (curated MITRE ATT&CK catalog from apate.attack).
operation.narrative_description: Combined scenario of network decoys and user behavior simulating the quarter-end close, a period of high legitimate activity.
operation.psychological_impact: The adversary believes the volume of legitimate quarter-close activity provides cover to exfiltrate data without detection.
operation.roles:
Operation lead: R. Sosa
Compliance officer: D. Molina
operation.resource_estimate: 3 analysts, 1 month, coordination with the legal team

scenario.description: Detect data exfiltration to external infrastructure after exploiting the exposed application

plugins.expected_adversary_belief: The backup decoy server contains the real quarter-close data.
plugins.expected_adversary_action: Exfiltrate the backup contents to external infrastructure.
plugins.success_metric: Detect outbound transfer to an unauthorized IP address.

plugins.expected_adversary_belief: The quarter-close operator is a real user with access to backups.
plugins.expected_adversary_action: Use that access to locate and exfiltrate the backup data.
plugins.success_metric: Detect backup access outside normal quarter-close hours.

plugins.expected_adversary_belief: The quarter-close transfer link exposes a real backup resource.
plugins.expected_adversary_action: Open the link and reuse the apparent infrastructure to locate the backup server.
plugins.success_metric: Record interaction with the breadcrumb before it reaches the network decoy.

plugins.expected_adversary_belief: The transfer host exposes administrative services for the financial backup.
plugins.expected_adversary_action: Enumerate SSH and FTP to prepare exfiltration from the closing environment.
plugins.success_metric: Detect the first connection attempt to the decoy host services.
